document.title: Signal/Synal Browser or Place: Setup Work Required and Current Position
document.summary: Signal/Synal should not be treated as a normal browser build. It is a signal-aware operating layer over existing browser infrastructure, combining extension shell, overlay, telemetry, Supabase state, queue/runtime execution, graph cognition, and governance receipts. The conceptual and governance layers are already strong; the remaining work is packaging, permissions, telemetry wiring, identity propagation, runtime linkage, recovery, and production hardening.
document.position: The organisation is not starting from zero. Prior work already defines the core concept, widget taxonomy, telemetry doctrine, Supabase spine, queue-first runtime model, signal tiles, and governance rules. The settings/configuration layer is manageable. The harder work sits in continuity, survivability, runtime truth, identity propagation, and graph integrity.

recommended_architecture.browser_base: Existing Chromium/Chrome/Edge rather than custom browser engine.
recommended_architecture.signal_layer: Extension family shell plus side panel and overlay.
recommended_architecture.context_capture: Content scripts, tab/session metadata, active page summaries, user-controlled capture.
recommended_architecture.truth_state: Supabase registry, runtime tables, audit/evidence ledger.
recommended_architecture.cognition: MRI/graph layer for continuity, relationships, unfinished loops, salience, risk, contradiction, priority, and reuse.
recommended_architecture.recovery: Queue replay, idempotency keys, worker receipts, telemetry continuity.
recommended_architecture.ux: Side panels, overlays, signal tiles, pinned actions, capture/reuse widgets.

settings_required: Capture permissions: tabs, activeTab, storage, optional history, clipboard only where justified.
Surface behaviour: overlay enabled, side panel enabled, signal tile mode, quiet mode.
Telemetry mode: local-only, hashed, summarised, synced, or full workspace mode.
Identity: workspace, user, session, device, browser profile, project routing.
AI routing: hosted model, local model, Bridge route, no-send private mode.
Runtime policies: auto-execute allowed, approval gate required, read-only mode, destructive-action block.
Signal retention: expiry, archive, promote-to-work, promote-to-asset, delete/archive separation.
Recovery: replay queues, restore session, retry failed execution, stale signal handling.
Sync: browser to Supabase to runtime to evidence ledger.
activation_backlog: Create extension manifest and shared shell package.
Create settings schema and defaults table.
Create Supabase event ingestion table or map to existing runtime/audit spine.
Create Peter/worker receipt watcher for this payload.
Create dashboard row showing enqueue, worker receipt, telemetry, recovery, and close state.
Create one local test: capture page signal -> queue job -> worker receipt -> evidence ledger.

work_required_table.reason: Needs clean schema and policy controls, not technically hard.
Needs reliable routing across browser, Supabase, runtime, users, devices.
Requires relationship modelling, summarisation, dedupe, and time continuity.
Event schema and ingestion are straightforward; governance quality matters.
Existing queue doctrine fits; worker execution and receipts must be hardened.
Idempotency, replay, stale detection, close signals, and worker receipts required.
Requires safe interpretation of intent, salience, repeated patterns, and context.
This is the actual strategic moat: living relationships, not static logs.
Must avoid surveillance framing and support enterprise trust.
Needs profile/device reconciliation and careful sync boundaries.
Needs permissions, policy, support, deployment, audit, and market positioning.

mvp_path.deliverable: Shared extension shell with branded side panel and popup.
Signal tile overlay for capture, classify, promote, archive.
Supabase telemetry ingestion with event schema and evidence states.
Queue/runtime linkage through Gateway/Bridge worker and receipt generation.
Browser session graph: tabs, domains, projects, signals, unfinished loops.
Cross-LLM continuity via Pen/Bridge receipt path and canonical summaries.
Autonomous recovery: retry, replay, stale detection, failed-run classification.
Persistent cognition fabric: graph-aware continuity across people, tools, places, and runtime.

governance_notes: Do not build a full browser engine first; use an extension/overlay/signal operating layer over existing Chromium surfaces.
Do not collect raw browsing data by default; summarise, classify, hash, and route with user/workspace policy.
Archive is not delete; signal lifecycle must preserve governance and evidence state.
REAL requires receipts: commit, worker execution, telemetry write, recovery proof, and visible runtime evidence.
PARTIAL is acceptable for design and enqueue; PRETEND is rejected for claims of runtime completion.
definition_of_done: Extension shell exists and loads locally or in controlled deployment.
Settings schema exists for permissions, telemetry, identity, AI routing, retention, recovery, and sync.
Events write to Supabase with evidence_state and idempotency_key.
Browser signal can create a queue job.
Worker can execute the job and write a receipt.
Receipt is linked back to the originating signal/session.
Governance dashboard can show REAL/PARTIAL/PRETEND state.

expected_worker_outputs: audit row or audit-compatible receipt reference
visible close signal if worker completes
failure receipt if trigger does not fire
receipt_requirements.close_condition: GitHub enqueue and update close on visible commit. Runtime remains open until Peter/worker emits receipt. If trigger does not fire, classify as PARTIAL with missing runtime receipt and raise trigger-path repair.
